_note: Lane decided the pairs and strengths on 2026-11-12 (LX1-LX5 kept as separate boxes, strengths as proposed). Spans are English numbering. strength: 3 shared words, 2 same story beat, 1 thematic. All are echo pairs.

sources.cite: Jacob Milgrom, Leviticus 1–16, Anchor Bible 3 (New York: Doubleday, 1991), p. 514 (table lining up the anointing in Exod 29:7, Exod 40:9–13 and Lev 8:10–12).
sources.what: Pointer for the anointing pair: Exod 29 has oil poured on Aaron only; Exod 40 anoints the tabernacle, furnishings and Aaron; Lev 8 anoints the tabernacle, sprinkles the altar, then pours oil on Aaron.
sources.boundary_note: Used only to point at the passages. The pairs and the shared words come from the verses.

sources.cite: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (morphhb: Westminster Leningrad Codex with Strong's-based lemmas), https://github.com/openscriptures/morphhb, pinned morphhb@2.0.2; English verse numbers via its VerseMap.xml.
sources.what: Every Strong's number in a `shared` entry was found in both cited verses by script.
sources.boundary_note: Lemma overlap shows shared vocabulary, not shared meaning; a shared word can be used in a different sense in each place.

pairs.title: Aaron and his sons ordained: the command, then the doing
pairs.strength_why: The ordination ram, the blood on ear, thumb and toe, and the wave offering use the same rare words in both.

beats.title: Gather the offerings at the door
Blood on right ear, thumb and toe
Fat, thigh and the wave offering
Boil the flesh at the door and eat

pairs.note: Exod 29 is the command; Lev 8 has Moses carry it out, nearly step for step. The one move Milgrom's table flags is the altar anointing (see LX2).

pairs.title: Washing, dressing and anointing: the tabernacle's order against Lev 8's
pairs.strength_why: The basin and its stand (kiyyor, ken) occur together in both verses, and the anointing verb runs through both.
pairs.note: Exod 29:7 has oil on Aaron's head only; Exod 40:9–13 anoints the dwelling and its vessels, the basin, then Aaron; Lev 8:10–12 anoints the dwelling, sprinkles the altar, anoints the altar, vessels, basin and stand, then Aaron. Pair for Lane: whether this and LX1 stay two boxes.

pairs.title: The first offerings in use: daily lambs against the eighth day
pairs.strength_why: Shared lamb, grain offering and oil are the vocabulary of any offering; what matches is the beat of the first regular offerings at the door, so same beat, not same wording.
pairs.note: Exod 29:38–42 sets the continual going up offering 'at the door of the tent of meeting'; Lev 9 is the first day it is offered after the ordination week.

pairs.title: 'My glory' meets Israel at the tent
pairs.strength_why: 'Glory' (kavod) and 'tent of meeting' sit in one verse on each side; Exod 29:43 promises it, Lev 9:23 records it.
pairs.note: A promise (Exod 29:43–46: I will meet the sons of Israel there, and it will be set apart by my glory) and its first sign (Lev 9:23–24).

pairs.title: The glory appears, the cloud covers
pairs.strength_why: Both end the setup with 'the glory of YHWH' and the tent of meeting; Lev 9:24 and Exod 40:38 both end on fire.
pairs.note: Moses cannot enter in Exod 40:35; in Lev 9:23 Moses and Aaron go in and come out. Pair for Lane: LX4 and LX5 share the same Leviticus verses and could be one box with two twins.
